domain: Monetary Economics / International Political Economy / Institutional History
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1971 Nixon Shock and the collapse of Bretton Woods, examining whether the gold-to-fiat transition was a discrete policy swap or an overdetermined composite of incompatible structural pressures. The research context frames this as a kernel contest: single-event reading vs. multi-pressure composite reading.

key_entities: President Richard Nixon (executive decision-maker, August 15 1971 announcement)
Bretton Woods System (1945-1971 fixed exchange rate regime)
Group of Ten (international negotiating bloc, Smithsonian Agreement Dec 1971)
Gold reserves (physical constraint on money supply)
U.S. dollar (reserve currency under Bretton Woods)
key_tensions: Domestic monetary flexibility vs. gold parity discipline (Fed policy space vs. $35/oz commitment)
International coordination vs. national sovereignty (Bretton Woods obligations vs. domestic growth priorities)
Capital mobility vs. fixed exchange rates (private cross-border flows vs. pegged currencies)
Inflation management vs. commodity backing (purchasing power erosion vs. gold value stability)
Reserve currency privilege vs. gold redemption obligation (dollar as global medium vs. convertibility drain)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The monetary regime commitment: what grounds the legitimacy and stability of the currency system
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Central banks and international monetary institutions claiming authority to define what constitutes sound money
commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: The supposed readings (single-swap vs. composite-pressure) do NOT emit different constraints—they are two analytical framings of the same historical rupture. A 'single swap' reading would still identify the same structural pressures (inflation, capital flows, coordination costs) as causal factors; it would merely claim they converged into one decision moment. A 'composite' reading identifies the same pressures as independently sufficient causes. Both readings observe the SAME constraint topology: the incompatibility between gold convertibility and the five structural demands cataloged in extraction. The disagreement is historiographic (was this overdetermined or contingent?) not structural (what constraints existed). This is a single constraint system read from different temporal/causal lenses, not multiple constraint systems from one kernel.

axes.structural_delta: Structural impossibility of maintaining gold convertibility, fixed exchange rates, and monetary policy autonomy simultaneously
axes.primary_observable: Central bank gold reserves vs. outstanding currency liabilities; capital account openness; domestic inflation rate vs. gold parity
axes.selection_reason: Mountain providing the physical/mathematical constraint base; highest inbound edge count from all other axes

axes.human_readable: Bretton Woods Coordination Costs (Multilateral Discipline Failure)
axes.structural_delta: Rising transaction costs of maintaining international monetary coordination as domestic policy priorities diverged
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of G10 negotiations; Smithsonian Agreement compliance rates; bilateral vs. multilateral policy coordination attempts
axes.selection_reason: Rope documenting the coordination mechanism that failed; structurally distinct from mountain (social vs. physical constraint)

axes.human_readable: Reserve Currency Extraction (Exorbitant Privilege as Structural Snare)
axes.structural_delta: U.S. ability to run persistent deficits by issuing reserve currency, creating asymmetric extraction from gold redemption obligations
axes.primary_observable: U.S. current account balance; foreign dollar holdings vs. U.S. gold reserves; Vietnam War + Great Society spending vs. gold coverage ratio
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; downstream synthesis node capturing the extraction dynamic that made the system unsustainable

axes.human_readable: Federal Reserve Mandate Drift (Employment Targeting vs. Gold Discipline)
axes.structural_delta: Post-1930s shift in Fed mandate from gold parity maintenance to domestic employment/growth stabilization
axes.primary_observable: Fed policy statements prioritizing employment vs. gold coverage; discount rate changes independent of gold flows
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: institutional drift captured indirectly via reserve_currency_extraction snare; lower structural distinctiveness

axes.structural_delta: Rising speed and volume of private cross-border capital flows undermining fixed exchange rate enforcement
axes.primary_observable: Cross-border capital flow volumes 1960s-1971; telecommunications infrastructure expansion; speculative attack frequency
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: technological mountain feeding into trilemma; already captured as one leg of the trilemma constraint

axes.human_readable: Inflation-Gold Parity Divergence (Purchasing Power Erosion vs. Fixed Metal Value)
axes.structural_delta: Domestic inflation eroding dollar purchasing power while gold parity remained fixed at $35/oz, creating arbitrage pressure
axes.primary_observable: U.S. CPI inflation rate 1960s-1971; gold market price vs. official $35/oz parity; London Gold Pool intervention frequency
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: tangled_rope captured as mechanism within reserve_currency_extraction; redundant with trilemma dynamics

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Fed mandate shift from gold parity to employment targeting
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Institutional drift captured indirectly via reserve_currency_extraction; lower graph centrality

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Technology-driven acceleration of cross-border capital flows
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Already incorporated as one leg of the trilemma mountain; redundant independent axis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Domestic inflation vs. fixed gold parity creating arbitrage pressure
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Mechanism subsumed within reserve_currency_extraction snare; overlapping observable with trilemma

omegas.description: The kernel contest (single-swap vs. composite) collapses because both readings observe the same constraint topology. The disagreement is historiographic (overdetermination vs. contingency) not structural (what constraints existed). This is NOT a contested kernel—it is one constraint system with two causal narratives.

Could the gold standard have been retained with different institutional design (e.g., adjustable parity, partial convertibility)? If yes, the Mountain classification of gold_convertibility_trilemma is weakened—it becomes a Piton of policy choice rather than physical necessity.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + F03 mountain validity check

omegas.description: Does fiat currency eliminate the trilemma or merely shift it? Modern central banks face inflation-credibility-growth trilemmas without gold. The 1971 transition may have swapped one mountain for another rather than eliminating constraint.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + structural persistence question

omegas.description: Post-1971, did the petrodollar system (oil priced in dollars) replace gold convertibility as the reserve currency anchor? If so, reserve_currency_extraction persists with different victims (oil importers vs. gold redeemers).
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (post-1971 monetary regime structure not analyzed)

omegas.description: The December 1971 Smithsonian Agreement attempted to preserve fixed rates without gold. Its rapid failure (by 1973) suggests the coordination_costs rope was already severed. Was this a genuine reform attempt or a face-saving scaffold?
omegas.source: Extraction anchor (Smithsonian Agreement) + scaffold hypothesis test

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: gold_convertibility_trilemma classified as mountain (physical/mathematical impossibility) but counterfactual institutional designs (adjustable parity, partial convertibility, capital controls) may have been viable. Generated omega_counterfactual_gold_retention to bound this uncertainty. The trilemma is a mountain given the Bretton Woods institutional design, but that design was a policy choice.
